rules.sentence: The treatment of systemic hypertension in MAS patients with WS includes calcium channel blockers, beta-blockers and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, and medical therapy is indicated in small children or in patients with unacceptable level of operative risk.
Combined antihypertensive treatment alone was used in half of children with MAS and WS.
Interventional treatment was used in the other half of the patients and in 20% of the patients vascular angioplasty was associated with renal auto-transplant.
Medical treatment, as has been demonstrated in other studies, has better results than interventional procedures.
ALGS is encountered in 1–8% of MAS cases.

Vascular abnormalities in ALGS include intracranial vascular abnormalities as aneurysm or moyamoya disease, which may lead to intracranial bleeding in up to 15% of cases and represents a major cause of morbidity and mortality in this disorder.
MAS was found in 1–2.4% of the individuals diagnosed with ALGS in a large study, but the association between ALGS and MAS is underestimated.
